title: Boss: the data desk
summary: Five real-looking analysis jobs that need every tool in the module: parsing, flattening, joins, deep grouping, sorting, reductions and a custom operator.

steps.title: Welcome to the data desk
body: Five requests have landed on your desk: server logs, a film catalogue, payroll, report cards and click streams. Each one is a small pipeline. The sixth is for you: your Sidekick's work sessions.
Before you type, say the pipeline out loud: *"parse, keep the errors, count per service, sort, take the top few."* Each phrase is an operator. Then write it.
No loops in the first four. The fifth asks you to build an operator of your own, and the last brings it home into `sk sessions`.

steps.title: Error hotspots
prompt: Log lines look like this:
```text
2024-03-01 10:15:02 ERROR Payments Timeout talking to bank
Split on spaces: the 3rd word is the **level**, the 4th is the **service**. Lines with fewer than 4 words are junk: skip them.

Write `static List<string> ErrorHotspots(List<string> lines, int top)`: count `ERROR` lines per service, most errors first, ties by service name A to Z, keep the first `top`, each as `"Payments: 3"`. No loops.
starter: static List<string> ErrorHotspots(List<string> lines, int top)
solution: static List<string> ErrorHotspots(List<string> lines, int top)
template: "2024-03-01 10:15:02 ERROR Payments Timeout talking to bank",
Dojo.Eq("all of them, ties by name", new List<string> { "Payments: 3", "Search: 2", "Auth: 1", "Billing: 1" }, ErrorHotspots(dojoLog, 10));
Dojo.Eq("a quiet day", new List<string>(), ErrorHotspots(new List<string> { "2024-03-01 09:00:00 INFO Web up" }, 3));
hints: Split each line once with `Select`, then work with the word arrays.
Sort the pairs with `OrderByDescending(p => p.Value).ThenBy(p => p.Key)`, then `Take(top)`.

steps.title: Genre report
prompt: The tests define `record Movie(string Title, int Year, double Rating, string[] Genres);` A film can be in several genres.
Write `static List<string> GenreReport(List<Movie> movies)`: one line per genre, sorted by genre, as
```text
Crime: 3 films, avg 7.9, best Heat
`avg` is the average rating with one decimal (`{x:0.0}`), `best` is the title of the highest-rated film in that genre (first one on a tie). No loops.
template: Dojo.Eq("one line per genre", new List<string>
Dojo.Eq("a film with no genres adds nothing", new List<string>(), GenreReport(new List<Movie> { new("Blank", 2000, 5.0, new string[0]) }));
record Movie(string Title, int Year, double Rating, string[] Genres);
hints: Flatten to (genre, movie) pairs first: `SelectMany(m => m.Genres, (m, genre) => new { genre, m })`.
Group by the genre with the movie as the element: `GroupBy(x => x.genre, x => x.m)`.

steps.title: Payroll against budget
prompt: The tests define:
```csharp
record Employee(string Name, int DeptId, decimal Salary);
record Department(int Id, string Name, decimal Budget);
Write two methods, no loops:

- `static List<string> Budgets(List<Employee> staff, List<Department> depts)`: **every** department, sorted by name, as `"IT: 160000 / 150000 OVER"`: total salaries, then the budget, then ` OVER` only if salaries are **more** than the budget. A department with no staff spends `0`.
- `static List<string> Unassigned(List<Employee> staff, List<Department> depts)`: names of staff whose `DeptId` matches no department, in list order.
starter: static List<string> Budgets(List<Employee> staff, List<Department> depts)
static List<string> Unassigned(List<Employee> staff, List<Department> depts)
solution: static List<string> Budgets(List<Employee> staff, List<Department> depts)
.GroupJoin(staff, d => d.Id, e => e.DeptId, (d, people) => new { d, Spent = people.Sum(e => e.Salary) })
static List<string> Unassigned(List<Employee> staff, List<Department> depts)
return staff.ExceptBy(depts.Select(d => d.Id), e => e.DeptId).Select(e => e.Name).ToList();
template: var dojoDepts = new List<Department> { new(1, "IT", 150000m), new(2, "Sales", 100000m), new(3, "Legal", 50000m) };
Dojo.Eq("every department, OVER only when over", new List<string> { "IT: 160000 / 150000 OVER", "Legal: 0 / 50000", "Sales: 100000 / 100000" }, Budgets(dojoStaff, dojoDepts));
Dojo.Eq("staff with no department", new List<string> { "Ed", "Fa" }, Unassigned(dojoStaff, dojoDepts));
Dojo.Eq("everyone assigned", new List<string>(), Unassigned(new List<Employee> { new("Ana", 1, 1m) }, dojoDepts));
record Employee(string Name, int DeptId, decimal Salary);
record Department(int Id, string Name, decimal Budget);
hints: `Join` would lose Legal. Every department once with its people is a `GroupJoin` from `depts`.
In the result selector, keep the department and `people.Sum(e => e.Salary)` (0 for nobody).
For `Unassigned`: `staff.ExceptBy(depts.Select(d => d.Id), e => e.DeptId)`, or a `Where` with `!ids.Contains(...)`. Careful: `ExceptBy` also removes repeats by key.

steps.title: Report cards
prompt: The tests define `record Score(string Student, string Subject, int Mark);` A student may have **retaken** a subject: only their **highest** mark in each subject counts.
Write `static List<string> ReportCards(List<Score> scores)`: one line per student, sorted by name:
```text
Bo: C (Music 79, Art 70, Math 70)
- subjects ordered by mark, highest first; equal marks by subject A to Z
- the letter comes from the average of the counted marks: 90 or more `A`, 80 or more `B`, 70 or more `C`, otherwise `F`
No loops.
template: Dojo.Eq("report cards, retakes counted once at their best", new List<string>
Dojo.Eq("no scores", new List<string>(), ReportCards(new List<Score>()));
record Score(string Student, string Subject, int Mark);
hints: First get one score per student and subject: group by `new { s.Student, s.Subject }` and keep `MaxBy(s => s.Mark)`.
Then group those by student and sort the groups by name.
Inside each student: sort the subjects for the text, and pass `g.Average(s => s.Mark)` to `Letter`.

steps.title: Click sessions
prompt: The tests define `record Click(string User, int Minute);` A **session** is a run of one user's clicks where each click is at most 30 minutes after the previous one. A gap of **more than 30** starts a new session.
Write a `static class Analytics` with:

1. A lazy extension method `SplitWhen<T>(this IEnumerable<T> source, Func<T, T, bool> split)` returning `IEnumerable<List<T>>`. It cuts the sequence between two neighbours `(prev, next)` whenever `split(prev, next)` is true. `[1, 2, 5, 6].SplitWhen((a, b) => b - a > 1)` is `[1, 2]`, `[5, 6]`. Use `yield return`.

2. `public static List<string> Sessions(List<Click> clicks)`: one line per user, sorted by user, as `"Ana: 2 sessions, longest 45 min"`. A session's length is its last minute minus its first. Clicks arrive in any order: sort each user's minutes first.
starter: public static IEnumerable<List<T>> SplitWhen<T>(this IEnumerable<T> source, Func<T, T, bool> split)
solution: public static IEnumerable<List<T>> SplitWhen<T>(this IEnumerable<T> source, Func<T, T, bool> split)
var sessions = g.Order().SplitWhen((a, b) => b - a > 30).ToList();
return $"{g.Key}: {sessions.Count} sessions, longest {sessions.Max(s => s[^1] - s[0])} min";
template: Dojo.Eq("SplitWhen on gaps", new List<string> { "1,2", "5,6" }, new[] { 1, 2, 5, 6 }.SplitWhen((a, b) => b - a > 1).Select(s => string.Join(",", s)).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("SplitWhen that never splits", 1, new[] { 1, 2, 3 }.SplitWhen((a, b) => false).Count());
Dojo.Eq("SplitWhen of nothing", 0, new int[0].SplitWhen((a, b) => true).Count());
Dojo.Eq("SplitWhen is lazy", new List<int> { 1, 2 }, Enumerable.Range(1, int.MaxValue).SplitWhen((a, b) => b % 3 == 0).First());
new("Bo", 7), new("Ana", 110), new("Ana", 5), new("Cy", 0), new("Ana", 50), new("Ana", 140),
Dojo.Eq("no clicks", new List<string>(), Analytics.Sessions(new List<Click>()));
hints: In `SplitWhen`, build the current piece in a list. Before adding an item, if the list is not empty and `split(current[^1], item)` is true, yield the list and start a new one.
Do not forget to yield the last piece after the loop.
In `Sessions`: `GroupBy(c => c.User, c => c.Minute)`, sort the groups, then for each `g.Order().SplitWhen((a, b) => b - a > 30).ToList()`; the longest is `Max(s => s[^1] - s[0])`.

steps.title: Sidekick: work sessions
prompt: **Sidekick piece, the last of this module.** `sk sessions` turns your activity of the day into work sessions, the way the click analytics did: any gap longer than `gap` starts a new session.
`static List<(DateTime Start, DateTime End)> Sessions(IEnumerable<DateTime> activity, TimeSpan gap)`
- sort the timestamps (they arrive in any order)

- one `Aggregate` whose seed is an empty `List<(DateTime Start, DateTime End)>`: if the list is not empty and the time is at most `gap` after the last session's `End`, stretch that session to this time; otherwise add a new session `(time, time)`
- a gap of exactly `gap` still joins
The tests also feed it the start and end of your `TimeEntry` records and print the lengths with your `Sk.FormatMinutes`.
starter: static List<(DateTime Start, DateTime End)> Sessions(IEnumerable<DateTime> activity, TimeSpan gap) =>
solution: static List<(DateTime Start, DateTime End)> Sessions(IEnumerable<DateTime> activity, TimeSpan gap) => activity
template: DateTime DojoAt(int h, int m) => new DateTime(2026, 11, 24, h, m, 0);
Dojo.Eq("two sessions, input unsorted", new List<(DateTime, DateTime)> { (DojoAt(9, 0), DojoAt(9, 25)), (DojoAt(10, 30), DojoAt(10, 40)) },
Sessions(new[] { DojoAt(10, 40), DojoAt(9, 10), DojoAt(9, 0), DojoAt(10, 30), DojoAt(9, 25) }, dojoGap));
Dojo.Eq("a gap of exactly 20 minutes joins", 1, Sessions(new[] { DojoAt(9, 0), DojoAt(9, 20) }, dojoGap).Count);
Dojo.Eq("21 minutes splits", 2, Sessions(new[] { DojoAt(9, 0), DojoAt(9, 21) }, dojoGap).Count);
Dojo.Eq("one moment is a session of zero length", new List<(DateTime, DateTime)> { (DojoAt(8, 0), DojoAt(8, 0)) }, Sessions(new[] { DojoAt(8, 0) }, dojoGap));
Dojo.Eq("no activity, no sessions", 0, Sessions(new List<DateTime>(), dojoGap).Count);
var dojoEntries = new List<TimeEntry> { new(1, DojoAt(9, 0), DojoAt(10, 30)), new(2, DojoAt(10, 40), DojoAt(11, 0)), new(1, DojoAt(14, 0), DojoAt(14, 45)) };
var dojoLengths = Sessions(dojoEntries.SelectMany(e => new[] { e.Start, e.End }), TimeSpan.FromHours(2)).Select(s => Sk.FormatMinutes((int)(s.End - s.Start).TotalMinutes)).ToList();
Dojo.Eq("sessions from your time entries (gap 2 h)", new List<string> { "2h 00m", "0h 45m" }, dojoLengths);
enum Status { Todo, Doing, Blocked, Done }
record TimeEntry(int TaskId, DateTime Start, DateTime End)
public static bool CanMove(Status from, Status to) => (from, to) switch
(Status.Doing, Status.Todo or Status.Blocked or Status.Done) => true,

require.message: Builds the sessions with one Aggregate

hints: `activity.Order().Aggregate(new List<(DateTime Start, DateTime End)>(), (sessions, time) => { ...; return sessions; })`.
`sessions[^1]` is the last session. Stretch it with `sessions[^1] = (sessions[^1].Start, time);`.
The join test is `sessions.Count > 0 && time - sessions[^1].End <= gap`.
steps.explain: An `Aggregate` with a list as its accumulator is a fold that builds a structure. It is the same idea as `SplitWhen`, written as a reduction instead of an iterator.

build.title: Work sessions
build.unlocks: `sk sessions` now turns your day into work sessions.
